pool.text: Diego Velázquez de Cuéllar founded the town of San Cristóbal de la Habana.
Havana originated adjacent to the port called Puerto de Carenas.
The Havana City Council was first created during the Governorate of Cuba.
Havana became the capital of the island, overtaking Santiago.
French corsair Jacques de Sores burned the city in its first attack.
A yellow fever epidemic killed one‑third of Havana’s population.
El Capitolio Nacional, the massive Senate and House building, was completed.
Ricardo Mira designed López Serrano Building, later a landmark
Bacardi Building completed as iconic Havana landmark
Teatro Warner Radiocentro opened with 1,650 seats
CM radio studio moved to Radiocentro building in El Vedado
CMQ‑TV launched on channel 6, becoming major Cuban broadcaster
Alicia Alonso founded the Ballet Nacional de Cuba.
Radiocentro CMQ Building constructed, showcasing modern architecture
The 20‑meter marble Christ of Havana statue was erected on the bay hillside.
Hilton Hotel opened, later housed Fidel Castro after revolution
Revolutionary government began expanding social services, public housing, and official buildings.
The United States imposed an embargo, causing severe shortages in Havana.
First International Festival of New Latin American Cinema held in Havana
Old Havana was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
